ImageDescription.value: Across coastal Karnataka and Udupi style vegetarian eateries throughout South India, Mangalore buns are an iconic breakfast and evening tea time snack, traditionally served alongside coconut chutney or vegetable sagu. To prepare them, overripe bananas are mashed with sugar, curd, a pinch of baking soda, and crushed cumin seeds, then kneaded with refined or whole wheat flour into a soft dough that is rested for several hours to ferment slightly. Small portions of the dough are rolled into thick discs and deep fried in hot oil until they puff up into golden, pillowy buns with a crisp exterior and a light, sweet interior.

The spots are not caused by a pathogen or pest, but appear naturally due to physiological changes that occur at an advanced stage of ripening (overripe, ripening stage 7 for banana). The spots may appear prematurely if the bananas are harvested at an advanced maturity stage and then subjected to forced ripening, and/or if the ripening parameters (i.e.,. the concentration of ethylene gas in the ripening chamber, the duration of exposure to ethylene gas, the air temperature during ripening) are excessive. 
Read: Banana ripening -- principles and practice (by S. Nelson) www.ctahr.hawaii.edu/nelsons/banana/ripeningbunchmanageme...

ImageDescription.value:
For her birthday, Persephone requested a "sun cake." I guess that's because she had a "moon cake" last year. Well, a sun cake would be round and yellow, sounds pretty easy. But she wanted this one to have sunflower seeds. A cake with sunflower seeds? Ye gods.

After searching around a bit I found a recipe. In retrospect I'd say it's really more of a quickbread than a cake, but it was quite delicious, if I do say so myself — especially with the blazing yellow buttercream icing. It sure didn't stick around long. It was almost gone before I could take this picture.

Recipe via Eating with Pebbles

Banana Sunflower Seed Cake

INGREDIENTS

2 medium overripe bananas 1 1/2 cups self-raising flour 1/4 tsp salt 1/4 tsp ground cinnamon 1/2 cup castor sugar 1/2 cup vegetable oil 1 cup water 1/4 cup sunflower seeds

METHOD

1. Preheat the oven to 180 degrees celsius.

2. Grease and flour an 8" round cake pan. Set aside.

3. Mash the bananas in a bowl. Set aside.

4. Sift the self-raising flour, salt and ground cinnamon in a bowl. Set aside.

5. Mix the sugar, oil and water in a mixing bowl using a hand whisk. Add the mashed bananas and sunflower seed and mix well.

6. Fold in the flour mixture using a wooden spatula and blend well.

7. Pour the batter into the prepared cake pan.

8. Bake for 35 minutes or until a skewer inserted in the middle of the cake comes out clean.
